children: , the global automotive and mobility powerhouse, climbed approximately 1.1% to $200.365 Thursday afternoon. Reuters reported that an auto-industry group representing Toyota and other major manufacturers is pressing Congress to ban Chinese vehicles, software and hardware from the United States before year-end.

The stakes are enormous for Toyota. North American revenue surged 14.9% to 6.11 trillion yen in its latest quarter, while regional operating income strengthened to 185.4 billion yen. Turning existing administrative restrictions into federal law could build a powerful barrier against heavily subsidized Chinese competitors.

North America produces roughly 45.1% of Toyota's quarterly revenue, making this protection push impossible for investors to ignore. The catch is cost: broader restrictions could disrupt sourcing and force expensive supply-chain changes. Toyota's stock also sits 6.36% below its $213.97 GF Value, leaving a noticeable valuation gap if the company can protect its biggest market without crushing margins.

title: Toyota Gains 1.1% as Automakers Push Congress to Ban Chinese Cars
